claim: The brainstem pre-Bötzinger complex (pre-BötC) region is located in the ventrolateral medulla oblongata.
source: The brainstem pre-Bötzinger complex (pre-BötC) region (Smith et al., 1991) located in the ventrolateral medulla oblongata is established to contain circuits essential for respiratory rhythm generation (Smith et al., 2013; Del Negro et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Smith et al., 1991.

claim: The pre-BötC is established to contain circuits essential for respiratory rhythm generation.
source: The brainstem pre-Bötzinger complex (pre-BötC) region (Smith et al., 1991) located in the ventrolateral medulla oblongata is established to contain circuits essential for respiratory rhythm generation (Smith et al., 2013; Del Negro et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Smith et al., 2013 and Del Negro et al., 2018.

claim: Pre-BötC excitatory neurons and circuits have autorhythmic properties and drive motor circuits that can be isolated and remain rhythmically active in living rodent brainstem slices in vitro.
source: Pre-BötC excitatory neurons and circuits have autorhythmic properties and drive motor circuits that can be isolated and remain rhythmically active in living rodent brainstem slices in vitro.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental observations in vitro preparations.

claim: Pharmacologically inhibiting INaP abolishes intrinsic neuronal rhythmic bursting in pre-BötC circuits.
source: INaP is proposed to mediate an essential oscillatory burst-generating mechanism since pharmacologically inhibiting INaP abolishes intrinsic neuronal rhythmic bursting as well as pre-BötC circuit inspiratory activity and rhythmic inspiratory motor output in vitro (Koizumi et al., 2008; Toporikova et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Pharmacologically inhibiting INaP abolishes pre-BötC circuit inspiratory activity in vitro.
source: INaP is proposed to mediate an essential oscillatory burst-generating mechanism since pharmacologically inhibiting INaP abolishes intrinsic neuronal rhythmic bursting as well as pre-BötC circuit inspiratory activity and rhythmic inspiratory motor output in vitro (Koizumi et al., 2008; Toporikova et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Pharmacologically inhibiting INaP abolishes rhythmic inspiratory motor output in vitro.
source: INaP is proposed to mediate an essential oscillatory burst-generating mechanism since pharmacologically inhibiting INaP abolishes intrinsic neuronal rhythmic bursting as well as pre-BötC circuit inspiratory activity and rhythmic inspiratory motor output in vitro (Koizumi et al., 2008; Toporikova et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: Intrinsic bursting in a subset of pre-BötC neurons in vitro was found to be terminated by the ICAN inhibitor flufenamic acid (FFA).
source: In the pre-BötC, ICAN was originally postulated to underlie intrinsic pacemaker-like oscillatory bursting at the cellular level and contribute to circuit-level rhythm generation, since intrinsic bursting in a subset of neurons in vitro was found to be terminated by the ICAN inhibitor flufenamic acid (FFA) (Peña et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Peña et al., 2004.

claim: Inhibition of ICAN in the pre-BötC reduces the amplitude of the rhythmic depolarization (inspiratory drive potential) driving neuronal bursting.
source: Furthermore, inhibition of ICAN in the pre-BötC reduces the amplitude of the rhythmic depolarization (inspiratory drive potential) driving neuronal bursting and can eliminate inspiratory motor activity in vitro (Pace et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Pace et al., 2007.

claim: Inhibition of ICAN in the pre-BötC can eliminate inspiratory motor activity in vitro.
source: Furthermore, inhibition of ICAN in the pre-BötC reduces the amplitude of the rhythmic depolarization (inspiratory drive potential) driving neuronal bursting and can eliminate inspiratory motor activity in vitro (Pace et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Pace et al., 2007.

claim: The molecular correlate of ICAN was postulated to be the transient receptor potential channel M4 (TRPM4).
source: The molecular correlate of ICAN was postulated to be the transient receptor potential channel M4 (TRPM4) (Mironov, 2008; Pace et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: TRPM4 and TRPC3 have been identified by immunolabeling and RNA expression profiling in pre-BötC inspiratory neurons in vitro.
source: TRPM4 and TRPC3 have now been identified by immunolabeling and RNA expression profiling in pre-BötC inspiratory neurons in vitro (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: Somatic calcium transients from voltage-gated sources do not contribute to the inspiratory drive potential.
source: Investigations into the sources of intracellular Ca2+ activating ICAN/TRPM4 suggested that (1) somatic calcium transients from voltage-gated sources do not contribute to the inspiratory drive potential (Morgado-Valle et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Morgado-Valle et al., 2008.

claim: IP3/ER-mediated intracellular Ca2+ release does not contribute to inspiratory rhythm generation in vitro.
source: Investigations into the sources of intracellular Ca2+ activating ICAN/TRPM4 suggested that (1) somatic calcium transients from voltage-gated sources do not contribute to the inspiratory drive potential (Morgado-Valle et al., 2008), (2) IP3/ER-mediated intracellular Ca2+ release does not contribute to inspiratory rhythm generation in vitro
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: In the dendrites calcium transients may be triggered by excitatory synaptic inputs and travel in a wave propagated to the soma.
source: and (3) in the dendrites calcium transients may be triggered by excitatory synaptic inputs and travel in a wave propagated to the soma (Mironov, 2008).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Mironov, 2008.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of ICAN/TRPM4 produces large reductions in the amplitude of pre-BötC inspiratory neuron population activity with essentially no, or minor perturbations of inspiratory rhythm.
source: Interestingly, pharmacological inhibition of ICAN/TRPM4 has been shown to produce large reductions in the amplitude of pre-BötC inspiratory neuron population activity with essentially no, or minor perturbations of inspiratory rhythm (Peña et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Peña et al., 2004.

claim: In the CaV network, increasing g-CAN has no effect on amplitude but increases the frequency of network oscillations.
source: In the CaV network, where calcium influx is generated exclusively from voltage-gated calcium channels, increasing g-CAN has no effect on amplitude but increases the frequency of network oscillations (Figure 1A, C, D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In the CaSyn network, increasing g-CAN strongly increases the amplitude and slightly decreases the oscillation frequency.
source: Conversely, in the CaSyn network where calcium influx is generated exclusively by excitatory synaptic input, increasing g-CAN strongly increases the amplitude and slightly decreases the oscillation frequency (Figure 1B, C, D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In INaP-dependent bursting neurons in the pre-BötC, bursting frequency depends on their excitability (i.e. baseline membrane potential).
source: In INaP-dependent bursting neurons in the pre-BötC, bursting frequency depends on their excitability (i.e. baseline membrane potential) which can be controlled in different ways, for example by directly injecting a depolarizing current (Smith et al., 1991; Del Negro et al., 2005; Yamanishi et al., 2018) or varying the conductance and/or reversal potentials of some ionic channels (Butera et al., 1999a).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: During the burst, INaP slowly inactivates resulting in burst termination and abrupt neuronal hyperpolarization.
source: During the burst, INaP slowly inactivates (Butera et al., 1999a) resulting in burst termination and abrupt neuronal hyperpolarization.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Butera et al., 1999a.

claim: In the CaV network, ICa as modeled remains residually activated between the bursts thus creating the background calcium concentration which partially activates ICAN.
source: In the CaV network, ICa as modeled remains residually activated between the bursts thus creating the background calcium concentration which partially activates ICAN.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model behavior.

claim: In the CaV network, between the bursts ICAN functions as a depolarizing leak current.
source: Therefore, between the bursts ICAN functions as a depolarizing leak current.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model behavior based on the residual activation of ICAN.

claim: In the CaV network increasing g-CAN increases ICAN, progressively depolarizing the network, which reduces the hNaP threshold for burst initiation and increases network oscillation frequency.
source: Consistently, we found that in the CaV network increasing g-CAN increases ICAN (Figure 2A), progressively depolarizing the network, which reduces the hNaP threshold for burst initiation (Figure 2B) and, thus, increases network oscillation frequency (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figures 1D and 2.

claim: In the CaSyn model, the intracellular calcium depletes entirely during the interburst interval.
source: In the CaSyn model, the intracellular calcium depletes entirely during the interburst interval.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model behavior.

claim: In the CaSyn model, increasing g-CAN has no effect on ICAN and frequency is essentially unaffected.
source: Consequently, increasing g-CAN has no effect on ICAN (Figure 2A) and frequency is essentially unaffected (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figures 1D and 2A.

claim: In the CaV network, increasing g-CAN increases the number of recruited neurons but decreases the average spiking frequency in recruited neurons, resulting in no change in amplitude.
source: In the CaV network, increasing g-CAN increases the number of recruited neurons (Figure 3A), but decreases the average spiking frequency in recruited neurons (Figure 3B) which, together result in no change in amplitude (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figures 1C and 3.

claim: In the CaSyn network, increasing g-CAN strongly increases the number of recruited neurons and increases the spike frequency of recruited neurons resulting in a large increase in network activity amplitude.
source: In the CaSyn network, increasing g-CAN strongly increases the number of recruited neurons (Figure 3A) and increases the spike frequency of recruited neurons (Figure 3B) resulting in a large increase in network activity amplitude (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The effects of varying g-CAN or the synaptic strength on network activity amplitude and frequency are qualitatively equivalent in the CaSyn network.
source: We found that the effects of varying g-CAN or the synaptic strength on network activity amplitude and frequency are qualitatively equivalent in the CaSyn network which is indicated by symmetry of the heat plots (across the X=Y line) in Figure 4A,B.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The effective strength of synaptic interactions in the network is roughly proportional to a product of the synaptic strength and g-CAN.
source: This symmetry results from the fact that the effective strength of synaptic interactions in the network is roughly proportional to a product of the synaptic strength and g-CAN.
evidence: This is a direct statement explaining the model behavior.

claim: Reducing either g-CAN or the synaptic strength have very similar effects on network activity amplitude and frequency.
source: We show that reducing either g-CAN or the synaptic strength have very similar effects on network activity amplitude and frequency (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: De-recruitment of neurons by reducing g-CAN or synaptic strength is nearly identical.
source: Furthermore, de-recruitment of neurons in both cases is nearly identical (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the CaSyn network, manipulations of g-CAN will affect the strength of the inspiratory drive potential in a way that is equivalent to changing the synaptic strength of the network.
source: Therefore, in the CaSyn network, manipulations of g-CAN will affect the strength of the inspiratory drive potential in the rhythmic inspiratory neurons in a way that is equivalent to changing the synaptic strength of the network.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model behavior.

claim: In the CaV network, manipulations of g-CAN will only slightly affect the inspiratory drive potential due to changes in the average firing rate of active neurons.
source: In contrast, manipulations of g-CAN in the CaV network will only slightly affect the inspiratory drive potential due to changes in the average firing rate of active neurons (see Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and references Figure 3B.

claim: Changing the synaptic connection probability and changing the strength of the calcium sources has no effect on the general relationship between g-CAN and the amplitude or frequency of bursts in the CaV or CaSyn networks.
source: We found that changing the synaptic connection probability and changing the strength of the calcium sources has no effect on the general relationship between g-CAN and the amplitude or frequency of bursts in the CaV or CaSyn networks.
evidence: This claim is directly stated about the robustness of the model results.

claim: The general effect of increasing g-CAN on amplitude and frequency is conserved in both networks regardless of the synaptic connection probability or strength of the calcium sources.
source: In other words, the general effect of increasing g-CAN on amplitude and frequency is conserved in both networks regardless of the synaptic connection probability or strength of the calcium sources.
evidence: This claim is directly stated about the robustness of the model results.

claim: Increasing the strength of the calcium sources affects the range of possible g-CAN values where both networks produce rhythmic activity.
source: Increasing the strength of the calcium sources does, however, affects the range of possible g-CAN values where both networks produce rhythmic activity.
evidence: This claim is directly stated about the model behavior.

claim: In the CaV model, increasing g-CAN increases frequency through increased excitability but has no effect on amplitude.
source: To summarize, in the CaV model, increasing g-CAN increases frequency, through increased excitability but has no effect on amplitude.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the model results.

claim: In the CaSyn model, increasing g-CAN slightly decreases frequency and increases amplitude.
source: In contrast, in the CaSyn model, increasing g-CAN slightly decreases frequency and increases amplitude.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the model results.

claim: In the CaSyn model, increasing g-CAN acts as a mechanism to increase the inspiratory drive potential and recruit previously silent neurons.
source: In this case, increasing g-CAN acts as a mechanism to increase the inspiratory drive potential and recruit previously silent neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model mechanism.

claim: The features of the CaV and CaSyn models are robust and conserved across a wide range of network parameters.
source: Additionally, these features of the CaV and CaSyn models are robust and conserved across a wide range of network parameters.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the robustness of the model results.

claim: In experiments where ICAN/TRPM4 was blocked by bath application of FFA or 9-phenanthrol in vitro, the amplitude of network oscillations was strongly reduced and their frequency remained unchanged or was reduced insignificantly.
source: In experiments where ICAN/TRPM4 was blocked by bath application of FFA or 9-phenanthrol (Koizumi et al., 2018) in vitro, the amplitude of network oscillations was strongly reduced and their frequency remained unchanged or was reduced insignificantly.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: If the calcium influx is exclusively voltage-gated, the model predicts that ICAN blockade will have no effect on amplitude but reduce the frequency.
source: If the calcium influx is exclusively voltage-gated, our model predicts that ICAN blockade will have no effect on amplitude but reduce the frequency.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a model prediction.

claim: If the calcium source is exclusively synaptically gated, the model predicts that blocking ICAN will strongly reduce the amplitude and slightly increase the frequency.
source: In contrast, if the calcium source is exclusively synaptically gated, our model predicts that blocking ICAN will strongly reduce the amplitude and slightly increase the frequency.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a model prediction.

claim: The best match to experimental data is observed if synaptically mediated and voltage-gated calcium influxes comprise about 95% and 5% of the total calcium influx, respectively.
source: We found that the best match is observed (Figure 7) if synaptically mediated and voltage-gated calcium influxes comprise about 95% and 5% of the total calcium influx, respectively.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: After decoupling the network (Wmax=0) a subset of neurons remained rhythmically active (7% in this simulation) and these were all neurons with a high INaP conductance.
source: We found that after decoupling the network (Wmax=0) a subset of neurons remained rhythmically active (7% in this simulation) and that these were all neurons with a high INaP conductance.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a simulation result.

claim: In rhythmically active neurons after network decoupling, bursting was abolished in all neurons by INaP blockade.
source: In these rhythmically active neurons, bursting was abolished in all neurons by INaP blockade.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a simulation result.

claim: ICa blockade applied before INaP block abolished intrinsic bursting in three of the seven neurons and INaP block applied afterwards abolished intrinsic bursting in the remaining four neurons.
source: Interestingly, ICa blockade applied before INaP block abolished intrinsic bursting in three of the seven neurons and INaP block applied afterwards abolished intrinsic bursting in the remaining four neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a simulation result.

claim: Although only one rhythmogenic (INaP-based) mechanism exists in this model, bursting in a subset of these intrinsically bursting neurons is calcium sensitive, consistent with experimental observations of calcium-sensitive intrinsic bursters.
source: Although only one rhythmogenic (INaP-based) mechanism exists in this model, bursting in a subset of these intrinsically bursting neurons is calcium sensitive, consistent with experimental observations of calcium-sensitive intrinsic bursters (Thoby-Brisson and Ramirez, 2001; Del Negro et al., 2005; Peña et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: In calcium-sensitive bursters, Ca2+ blockade in the model abolishes bursting by reducing the intracellular calcium concentration and, hence, ICAN activation, which ultimately reduces excitability.
source: In calcium-sensitive bursters, Ca2+ blockade in our model abolishes bursting by reducing the intracellular calcium concentration and, hence, ICAN activation, which ultimately reduces excitability.
evidence: This is a direct statement explaining the model mechanism.

claim: The neurons that remain active after ICAN blockade are primarily neurons with the highest g-NaP and bursting in these neurons is dependent on INaP.
source: We found that the neurons that remain active are primarily neurons with the highest g-NaP and that bursting in these neurons is dependent on INaP.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a simulation result.

claim: The neurons that remain active after complete blockade of ICAN form a INaP-dependent kernel of a rhythm generating circuit.
source: These neurons that remain active after compete blockade of ICAN form a INaP-dependent kernel of a rhythm generating circuit.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a model conclusion.

claim: Dynamic calcium imaging has been used to assess activity of the population of pre-BöC excitatory neurons as well as individual pre-BötC neurons during pharmacological inhibition of ICAN/TRPM4 in vitro.
source: Dynamic calcium imaging has been used to assess activity of the population of pre-BöC excitatory neurons as well as individual pre-BötC neurons during pharmacological inhibition of ICAN/TRPM4 in vitro (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: Network output activity amplitude and pre-BötC excitatory population-level intracellular calcium transients are highly correlated while the network oscillation frequency is not significantly perturbed during ICAN/TRPM4 inhibition.
source: These experiments indicate that network output activity amplitude and pre-BötC excitatory population-level intracellular calcium transients are highly correlated while the network oscillation frequency is not significantly perturbed.
evidence: This claim is directly stated about experimental observations.

claim: During ICAN/TRPM4 block, changes in calcium transients of individual neurons can differ significantly from the average population-level calcium transients.
source: Interestingly, during ICAN/TRPM4 block, changes in calcium transients of individual neurons can differ significantly from the average population-level calcium transients.
evidence: This claim is directly stated about experimental observations.

claim: Regardless of PSyn, the network activity amplitude and average intracellular calcium concentration are highly correlated.
source: We found that regardless of PSyn, the network activity amplitude and average intracellular calcium concentration are highly correlated (Figure 10A,B).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 10.

claim: PSyn affects the change in the peak Cai in individual neurons.
source: PSyn does, however, affect the change in the peak Cai in individual neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a simulation result.

claim: In a network with a high connection probability (PSyn=1) the synaptic current/calcium transient is nearly identical for all neurons and therefore the change in Cai during ICAN blockade is approximately the same for each neuron.
source: In a network with a high connection probability (PSyn=1) the synaptic current/calcium transient is nearly identical for all neurons and therefore the change in Cai during ICAN blockade is approximately the same for each neuron (Figure 10C).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: In a sparsely connected network, the synaptic current and calcium influx are more variable and reflect the heterogeneity in spiking frequency of the pre-synaptic neurons.
source: In a sparsely connected network, as proposed for the connectivity of the pre-BötC network (Carroll et al., 2013; Carroll and Ramirez, 2013) the synaptic current and calcium influx are more variable and reflect the heterogeneity in spiking frequency of the pre-synaptic neurons (Figure 10).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 10 and citations.

claim: In a network with low connection probability (PSyn<0.1), the peak Cai transient in some neurons increases when ICAN is blocked, consistent with experimental results.
source: Interestingly, in a network with low connection probability (PSyn<0.1), the peak Cai transient in some neurons increases when ICAN is blocked (Figure 10E), consistent with our experimental results (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 10E and citation to experimental results.

claim: Distinct biophysical mechanisms are involved in generating the rhythm and amplitude of inspiratory oscillations in the isolated pre-BötC excitatory circuits.
source: Based on our computational model, distinct biophysical mechanisms are involved in generating the rhythm and amplitude of inspiratory oscillations in the isolated pre-BötC excitatory circuits.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Inspiratory rhythm generation arises from a group of INaP-dependent excitatory neurons, including cells with intrinsic oscillatory bursting properties, that form a rhythmogenic kernel.
source: According to this model, inspiratory rhythm generation arises from a group of INaP-dependent excitatory neurons, including cells with intrinsic oscillatory bursting properties, that form a rhythmogenic kernel.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Rhythmic synaptic drive from rhythmogenic kernel neurons triggers post-synaptic calcium transients, ICAN activation, and subsequent membrane depolarization which drives rhythmic bursting in the rest of the population of inspiratory neurons.
source: Rhythmic synaptic drive from these neurons triggers post-synaptic calcium transients, ICAN activation, and subsequent membrane depolarization which drives rhythmic bursting in the rest of the population of inspiratory neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Activation of ICAN by synaptically-driven calcium influx functions as a mechanism that amplifies the excitatory synaptic input to generate the inspiratory drive potential and population activity amplitude in non-rhythmogenic neurons.
source: We showed that activation of ICAN by synaptically-driven calcium influx functions as a mechanism that amplifies the excitatory synaptic input to generate the inspiratory drive potential and population activity amplitude in these non-rhythmogenic neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Reduction of ICAN causes a robust decrease in overall network activity amplitude via de-recruitment of burst amplitude-generating neurons without substantial perturbations of the inspiratory rhythm.
source: Consequently, reduction of ICAN causes a robust decrease in overall network activity amplitude via de-recruitment of these burst amplitude-generating neurons without substantial perturbations of the inspiratory rhythm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study.

claim: ICAN plays a critical role in generating the amplitude of rhythmic population activity, which is consistent with the results from experimental inhibition of ICAN/TRPM4 channels.
source: Thus, ICAN plays a critical role in generating the amplitude of rhythmic population activity, which is consistent with the results from experimental inhibition of ICAN/TRPM4 channels (Peña et al., 2004; Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study with citations to supporting experimental work.

claim: The model provides a theoretical explanation for experimental results showing large reductions in amplitude with ICAN/TRPM4 blockade and provides new insights into the biophysical operation of pre-BötC excitatory circuits.
source: Our model provides a theoretical explanation for these experimental results and new insights into the biophysical operation of pre-BötC excitatory circuits.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the contribution of the study.

claim: The model describes a network of N=100 synaptically coupled excitatory neurons.
source: The model describes a network of N=100 synaptically coupled excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model structure.

claim: Simulated neurons are comprised of a single compartment described using a Hodgkin Huxley formalism.
source: Simulated neurons are comprised of a single compartment described using a Hodgkin Huxley formalism.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model structure.

claim: Gradual blockade of synaptic interactions by low calcium solution significantly decreases network activity amplitude while having little effect on frequency.
source: This is the case as Johnson et al. (1994) showed that gradual blockade of synaptic interactions by low calcium solution significantly decreases network activity amplitude while having little effect on frequency, similar to the experiments where the ICAN channel TRPM4 is blocked with 9-phenanthrol (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Johnson et al. (1994) and Koizumi et al. (2018).

claim: Complete blockade of ICAN in the model can ultimately abolish synchronized network oscillations due to weakened excitatory synaptic transmission, which results in neuronal de-recruitment and desynchronization of the network, particularly when synaptic strength is low.
source: We note that complete blockade of ICAN in our model can ultimately abolish synchronized network oscillations due to weakened excitatory synaptic transmission, which results in neuronal de-recruitment and desynchronization of the network, particularly when synaptic strength is low (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model behavior with reference to Figure 4.

claim: ICAN plays a critical role in network activity synchronization that determines the ability of the pre-BötC excitatory network to produce rhythmic output, depending on synaptic strength.
source: Thus, ICAN plays a critical role in network activity synchronization that determines the ability of the pre-BötC excitatory network to produce rhythmic output, depending on synaptic strength.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a model conclusion.

claim: The role of ICAN/TRPM4 activation is to amplify excitatory synaptic drive in generating the amplitude of inspiratory population activity, essentially independent of the biophysical mechanism generating inspiratory rhythm.
source: Overall, our new model simulations for the isolated pre-BötC excitatory network suggest that the role of ICAN/TRPM4 activation is to amplify excitatory synaptic drive in generating the amplitude of inspiratory population activity, essentially independent of the biophysical mechanism generating inspiratory rhythm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study.

claim: In the more intact brainstem respiratory network that ordinarily generates patterns of inspiratory and expiratory activity, endogenous activation of ICAN/TRPM4 appears to augment the amplitude of both inspiratory and expiratory population activity.
source: We note that the recent experiments have also shown that in the more intact brainstem respiratory network that ordinarily generates patterns of inspiratory and expiratory activity, endogenous activation of ICAN/TRPM4 appears to augment the amplitude of both inspiratory and expiratory population activity, and hence these channels are fundamentally involved in inspiratory-expiratory pattern formation (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: ICAN/TRPM4 channels are fundamentally involved in inspiratory-expiratory pattern formation.
source: We note that the recent experiments have also shown that in the more intact brainstem respiratory network that ordinarily generates patterns of inspiratory and expiratory activity, endogenous activation of ICAN/TRPM4 appears to augment the amplitude of both inspiratory and expiratory population activity, and hence these channels are fundamentally involved in inspiratory-expiratory pattern formation (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: Intracellular calcium transients are highly correlated with network and cellular activity across the duration of an ICAN blockade simulation, consistent with experimental observations.
source: We show that intracellular calcium transients are highly correlated with network and cellular activity across the duration of an ICAN blockade simulation, consistent with experimental observations.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a model result consistent with experimental observations.

claim: In a subset of neurons the peak calcium transient increases with reduced ICAN, which is supported by calcium imaging data.
source: Additionally, we examined the relative change in the peak calcium transients in single neurons as a function of ICAN conductance. We show that in a subset of neurons the peak calcium transient increases with reduced ICAN. This result is surprising but is also supported by the calcium imaging data (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to calcium imaging data.

claim: In pacemaker neurons, ICAN blockade leads to a reduction of their excitability resulting in an increased value of INaP inactivation gating variable at the burst onset.
source: In pacemaker neurons, ICAN blockade leads to a reduction of their excitability resulting in an increased value of INaP inactivation gating variable at the burst onset.
evidence: This is a direct statement explaining the model mechanism.

claim: During the burst, the peak action potential frequency and the synaptic output from pacemaker neurons is increased with ICAN blockade.
source: Thus, during the burst, the peak action potential frequency and the synaptic output from these neurons is increased with ICAN blockade.
evidence: This is a direct statement explaining the model mechanism.

claim: Neurons that receive synaptic input from pacemaker neurons will see an increase in their peak calcium transients with ICAN blockade.
source: Consequently, neurons that receive synaptic input from pacemaker neurons will see an increase in their peak calcium transients.
evidence: This is a direct statement explaining the model mechanism.

claim: In most neurons, synaptic input is received primarily from non-pacemaker rhythmic neurons.
source: In most neurons, however, synaptic input is received primarily from non-pacemaker rhythmic neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model structure.

claim: Since ICAN blockade de-recruits non-pacemaker neurons, the synaptic input and subsequent calcium influx in most cells decreases.
source: Since ICAN blockade de-recruits these non-pacemaker neurons, the synaptic input and subsequent calcium influx in most of these cells decreases.
evidence: This is a direct statement explaining the model mechanism.

claim: In a sparse network, blocking ICAN results in very diverse responses at the cellular level with an overall tendency to reduce intracellular calcium transients such that the amplitude of these transients averaged over the entire population decreases during ICAN blockade, while their burst frequency is essentially unchanged.
source: Therefore, our model predicts that in a sparse network, which has been proposed for pre-BötC network connectivity (Carroll et al., 2013; Carroll and Ramirez, 2013), blocking ICAN results in very diverse responses at the cellular level with an overall tendency to reduce intracellular calcium transients such that the amplitude of these transients averaged over the entire population decreases during ICAN blockade, while their burst frequency is essentially unchanged, as found from the calcium imaging experiments (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement of a model prediction with citations to supporting experimental work.

claim: There are three subtypes of ionotropic glutamate receptors: N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA), Kainate (KAR), and a-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA), all of which are expressed in the pre-BötC.
source: There are three subtypes of ionotropic glutamate receptors, N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA), Kainate (KAR), and a-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA), all of which are expressed in the pre-BötC (Paarmann et al., 2000) and have varying degrees of calcium permeability.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Paarmann et al., 2000.

claim: Pharmacological blockade of NMDA receptors does not consistently effect the amplitude or frequency of XII motor output.

claim: The KAR subunit GluK3 is highly expressed in the pre-BötC and is calcium permeable making it a possible candidate for synaptically mediated calcium entry.
source: The KAR subunit GluK3 is highly expressed in the pre-BötC (Paarmann et al., 2000) and is calcium permeable (Perrais et al., 2009) making it a possible candidate for synaptically mediated calcium entry.

claim: GluK3 is insensitive to tonic glutamate release and only activated by large glutamate transients.

claim: Group 1 mGluRs which include mGluR1 and mGluR5 are typically located on post-synaptic terminals.

evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Shigemoto et al., 1997.

claim: Activation of group 1 mGluRs is commonly associated with calcium influx through calcium permeable channels.
source: and activation of group 1 mGluRs is commonly associated with calcium influx through calcium permeable channels (Berg et al., 2007; Endoh, 2004; Mironov, 2008) and calcium release from intracellular calcium stores (Pace et al., 2007).

claim: In the pre-BötC, mGluR1/5 are thought to contribute to calcium influx by triggering the release of calcium from intracellular stores.
source: In the pre-BötC, mGluR1/5 are thought to contribute to calcium influx by triggering the release of calcium from intracellular stores (Pace et al., 2007)

claim: In the pre-BötC, mGluR1/5 are thought to contribute to calcium influx by the activation of the transient receptor potential C3 (TRPC3) channel.
source: In the pre-BötC, mGluR1/5 are thought to contribute to calcium influx by triggering the release of calcium from intracellular stores (Pace et al., 2007) and/or the activation of the transient receptor potential C3 (TRPC3) channel (Ben-Mabrouk and Tryba, 2010).

claim: Blockade of mGluR1/5 reduces the inspiratory drive potential in pre-BötC neurons without significant perturbation of inspiratory frequency.

claim: TRPC3 is a calcium permeable channel that is associated with calcium signaling.
source: TRPC3 is a calcium permeable channel (Thebault et al., 2005) that is associated with calcium signaling (Hartmann et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: TRPC3 is associated with store-operated calcium entry.
source: TRPC3 is a calcium permeable channel (Thebault et al., 2005) that is associated with calcium signaling (Hartmann et al., 2011), store-operated calcium entry (Kwan et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Kwan et al., 2004.

claim: TRPC3 is associated with synaptic transmission.
source: TRPC3 is a calcium permeable channel (Thebault et al., 2005) that is associated with calcium signaling (Hartmann et al., 2011), store-operated calcium entry (Kwan et al., 2004), and synaptic transmission (Hartmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Hartmann et al., 2011.

claim: TRPC3 is activated by diacylglycerol (DAG).
source: TRPC3 is activated by diacylglycerol (DAG) (Clapham, 2003), which is formed after synaptic activation of mGluR1/5.

claim: TRPC3 is highly expressed in pre-BötC glutamatergic inspiratory neurons and is often co-expressed with TRPM4.

evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: TRPC3 was hypothesized to underlie ICAN activation in the pre-BötC.

claim: TRPC3 and ICAN have been shown to underlie slow excitatory post-synaptic current (sEPSC).
source: Furthermore, TRPC3 and ICAN have been shown to underlie slow excitatory post-synaptic current (sEPSC) (Hartmann et al., 2008; Hartmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: The effect of TRPC3 blockade by 3-pyrazole on pre-BötC network activity amplitude is remarkably similar to that with blockade of TRPM4.
source: The effect of TRPC3 blockade by 3-pyrazole on pre-BötC network activity amplitude is remarkably similar to that with blockade of TRPM4 (Koizumi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Koizumi et al., 2018.

claim: INaP is a conductance present ubiquitously in pre-BötC inspiratory neurons.
source: INaP is a conductance present ubiquitously in pre-BötC inspiratory neurons, and is established to underlie intrinsic oscillatory neuronal bursting in the absence of excitatory synaptic interactions in neurons with sufficiently high INaP conductance densities (Del Negro et al., 2002; Koizumi and Smith, 2008; Koizumi and Smith, 2008; Yamanishi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: INaP is established to underlie intrinsic oscillatory neuronal bursting in the absence of excitatory synaptic interactions in neurons with sufficiently high INaP conductance densities.
source: INaP is a conductance present ubiquitously in pre-BötC inspiratory neurons, and is established to underlie intrinsic oscillatory neuronal bursting in the absence of excitatory synaptic interactions in neurons with sufficiently high INaP conductance densities (Del Negro et al., 2002; Koizumi and Smith, 2008; Koizumi and Smith, 2008; Yamanishi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: The circuit neurons mostly with relatively high INaP conductance values underlie rhythm generation and remain active after complete blockade of ICAN in the model network, thus forming a INaP-dependent rhythmogenic kernel.
source: Our simulations indicate that the circuit neurons mostly with relatively high INaP conductance values underlie rhythm generation and remain active after compete blockade of ICAN in our model network, thus forming a INaP-dependent rhythmogenic kernel, including some neurons with intrinsic oscillatory bursting behavior when synaptically uncoupled.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a simulation result.

claim: The rhythmogenic properties of individual neurons depend on whether their INaP conductance is high enough and, therefore, the number of intrinsic bursters in the model is defined by the width of this conductance distribution over the population.
source: As noted above, the rhythmogenic properties of individual neurons depend on whether their INaP conductance is high enough and, therefore, the number of intrinsic bursters in the model is defined by the width of this conductance distribution over the population.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the model structure.

claim: The critical value of INaP conductance and intrinsic bursting properties in general were shown theoretically and experimentally to critically depend on the conductances of other ionic channels and extracellular ion concentrations such as potassium concentration.
source: However, the critical value of INaP conductance and intrinsic bursting properties in general were also shown theoretically and experimentally to critically depend on the conductances of other ionic channels (e.g. leak and delayed rectifier potassium conductances) and extracellular ion concentrations such as potassium concentration (Bacak et al., 2016b; Koizumi and Smith, 2008; Rybak et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: There is functional heterogeneity within pre-BötC excitatory circuits, including distinct subpopulations of neurons involved in generating periodic sighs, arousal, and the subpopulations generating regular inspiratory activity.
source: Recently, it has become apparent that there is functional heterogeneity within pre-BötC excitatory circuits, including distinct subpopulations of neurons involved in generating periodic sighs (Toporikova et al., 2015; Li et al., 2016), arousal (Yackle et al., 2017), and the subpopulations generating regular inspiratory activity.
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: Activity of the normal inspiratory and sigh-generating subpopulations in the pre-BötC isolated in vitro is proposed to be dependent on activation of INaP.
source: Activity of the normal inspiratory and sigh-generating subpopulations in the pre-BötC isolated in vitro is proposed to be dependent on activation of INaP (Toporikova et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Toporikova et al., 2015.

claim: Within the normal inspiratory population, there are subpopulations distinguished by their role in rhythm versus amplitude generation due to biophysical properties: there is a ICAN/TRPM4-dependent recruitable population of excitatory neurons for burst amplitude generation and the INaP-dependent rhythmogenic kernel population.
source: Our experimental and modeling results suggest that within the normal inspiratory population, there are subpopulations distinguished by their role in rhythm versus amplitude generation due to biophysical properties: there is a ICAN/TRPM4-dependent recruitable population of excitatory neurons for burst amplitude generation and the INaP-dependent rhythmogenic kernel population.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a main conclusion of the study.

claim: A 'burstlet theory' for emergent network rhythms has recently been proposed to account for inspiratory rhythm and pattern generation in the isolated pre-BötC in vitro.
source: A 'burstlet theory' for emergent network rhythms has recently been proposed to account for inspiratory rhythm and pattern generation in the isolated pre-BötC in vitro (Kam et al., 2013; Del Negro et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: The burstlet theory postulates that a subpopulation of excitatory neurons generating small amplitude oscillations (burstlets) functions as the inspiratory rhythm generator that drives neurons that generate the larger amplitude, synchronized inspiratory population bursts.
source: This theory postulates that a subpopulation of excitatory neurons generating small amplitude oscillations (burstlets) functions as the inspiratory rhythm generator that drives neurons that generate the larger amplitude, synchronized inspiratory population bursts.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the burstlet theory.

claim: A basic property of INaP is its ability to generate subthreshold oscillations and promote burst synchronization.
source: We also note that a basic property of INaP is its ability to generate subthreshold oscillations and promote burst synchronization (Butera et al., 1999b; Bacak et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: In the isolated pre-BötC including in more mature rodent experimental preparations in situ, inspiratory rhythm generation has been shown to be dependent on INaP.
source: We emphasize that the above discussions regarding the role of INaP pertain to the excitatory circuits in the isolated pre-BötC including in more mature rodent experimental preparations in situ where inspiratory rhythm generation has also been shown to be dependent on INaP (Smith et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is directly stated and supported by citation to Smith et al., 2007.
